description:
FILED s427 (Opus), as the named residue of #415 item 1.

s427 made `@?` and its CL-SAFE siblings work: Pl::Parser::_merge_punct_array_symbols
merges PPI's Cast('@') + Operator(X) back into one Symbol, and Parser2's
punctuation forward-declaration bucket declares the whole family instead of
`@#` alone.  The set it covers is %PUNCT_ARRAY_CHARS = `? ! . / ~ ^ & % = < >`.

THE BOUNDARY IS THE CL SYMBOL SPELLING, NOT PERL.  Those ten characters are CL
constituents, so `@?` reads BARE exactly as the synthesized `@#` already does.
The rest of perl's punctuation names are CL macro or escape characters and
would need a pipe-quoted symbol (`|@,|`), which is a separate emission rule —
and one that sits in #418's territory (the non-ASCII pipe-quoting rule), so it
should be taken WITH that work rather than beside it.

MEASURED (perl 5.40.3): every punctuation character names a legal array except
`+` and `-` (read-only magic) and `{` (a syntax error):

    @, @; @| @' @" @` @( @) @[ @] @} @$ @@ @# @\ @: @*   all OK
    @+ @-   "Modification of a read-only value attempted"
    @{      syntax error

PPI lexes them variously — Cast + Operator (the fixed family), Cast +
Structure (`@;` `@(` `@[`), Cast + Quote (`@'` `@"` `@\``), Cast + Cast
(`@\` `@@`), Symbol (`@:` — already whole), Magic (`@*` `@+` `@-`).

The `%` sigil is a SEPARATE and riskier axis: PPI does not even produce a Cast
for `%?` — it gives Operator('%') + Operator('?'), i.e. a modulus — so a
merge there cannot use "a cast cannot abut an operator" as its licence.
`%!` and `%+`/`%-` are Magic and already work.

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR: these spellings DROP, loudly (the #339 announcement), which
is the status quo and is not silent.  ZERO corpus rows depend on them
(measured s427 over perl-tests/, perl's t/, lib/** and cpan-tests/modules).

REPRODUCER:
    @, = (1,2); print scalar(@,), "\n";   # perl: 2   PCL: statement dropped


UNBLOCKED s446j (agent J, while fixing #506): the stated blocker -- "the rest of perl's punctuation names would need a pipe-quoted spelling, which is its own emission rule" -- is FALSE as of PPI 1.291's emitter: cl_name/cl_sym already pipe-quote them (|@,| |@;| |@\|| |@"|, verified symbol by symbol from the emission), and s446j made the RUNTIME own every punctuation array AND hash perl allows (measured char by char).  So widening Pl::Parser::%PUNCT_ARRAY_CHARS to the full set is now a token-repair question only.  The HASH twin of the same repair is task #550, and it is the harder half (`%` is ambiguous with modulo, `@` is not).
title: Punctuation-named globals whose CL symbol spelling needs pipe quoting still DROP (`@,` `@;` `@|` `@'` `@"` `@(`), and the `%X` hash family is untouched
